key_insight: LLM agents with tool-calling can turn household preferences, prices, weather, and solar forecasts into near-optimal home energy schedules.
engineering_relevance: This shows a practical pathway for deploying natural-language interfaces in home energy management to improve cost savings, demand response, and appliance scheduling.
method: Built a ReAct-style tool-calling agent for multi-appliance scheduling.
Integrated live Octopus Agile prices, weather forecasts, PV generation estimates, usage data, and retrieval-augmented knowledge.
Benchmarked GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 against MILP ground truth and a week-long oracle baseline.
evidence_signal: Across tariff, conflict, weather-aware solar, and week-long tests, native function calling achieved 100% scheduling success and 96.7–98.0% of oracle savings.
watch_item: Performance drops sharply when actions must be text-parsed instead of natively function-called, so deployment quality depends on robust tool integration.
paper_title: LLMs for Agentic Home Energy Management
